clue.text: To leave university is a disappointment

definitions.meaning: to ... is the British phrase for leaving Oxford or Cambridge at the end of study
a letdown or anticlimax, a fall from a higher state

explanation.surface: A grumbler insists that quitting one's degree course is a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a student 'goes up' to university and 'comes down' on leaving it, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb phrase for leaving university, and the noun for a letdown or anticlimax.

clue.text: In travelling bag male has single shirt

indicators.note: In says the following letters sit inside the bag word

parts.note: a case is a suitcase
I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: A bachelor's suitcase contains just one shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose shirt or shift, often worn as an undergarment, is a kind of shirt.

clue.text: Book Premiership players (Arsenal's wingers)

parts.note: Man U is Manchester United, a Premier League football club

indicators.note: wingers are the players on the flanks, so take the outside letters

explanation.surface: A book about Premier League footballers and Arsenal's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United are an English football club; the Premiership is England's top league.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbook giving instructions is a book of guidance.

clue.text: Sweeties about to be put on top of a certain sort of cake

indicators.text: to be put on top of
indicators.note: to be put on top of places the earlier pieces above the last in this down entry

parts.note: drops are small boiled sweets, British sweeties
C is circa, about
one as in 'a certain person', one man

explanation.surface: Sweets are about to be added as topping on a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A drop scone is a small thick pancake, called a Scotch pancake in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small griddle cake of batter dropped onto a hot surface is a kind of cake.

clue.text: Eager to absorb one American or British author

indicators.note: to absorb says the eager word takes in the other pieces

parts.note: willing means eager, ready
I is the Roman numeral one
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Keen to take in one writer, American or British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' reads as a conjunction but is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Lord of the Flies was an English novelist and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Potentially lousy sort in school?

indicators.note: in says the egg word sits inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: a nit is a louse egg, so it is a louse in waiting

explanation.surface: A question about a pupil who might pick up head lice at school.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a playground telltale, a nasty sort found in school; the question mark flags that 'lousy' plays on head lice.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale who informs on classmates is a contemptible, lousy sort typically met in the schoolyard.

clue.text: One's uncovered declaration of independence in Newcastle area

indicators.note: in places the declaration inside the area

parts.note: NE is north-east England, where Newcastle lies
UDI is a unilateral declaration of independence, as Rhodesia made in 1965

explanation.surface: A political declaration of independence is revealed in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's uncovered' reads as revealed, but means a person or picture with no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for something featuring naked bodies, such as a film or magazine, where someone is bare.

clue.text: Making pie, measure salt

parts.note: a tart is a pastry pie
a rate is a measure, as of speed

explanation.surface: A cook making a pie measures out some salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt or ester of tartaric acid, as found in wine deposits, is a chemical salt.

clue.text: Some cars in Derby, say, will bypass road works

indicators.note: will bypass says the hat goes round the road abbreviation

parts.note: a derby is an American bowler hat, an example of a hat
ops are operations, works

explanation.surface: Traffic in Derby will avoid the roadworks.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby reads as the English city; it is the American name for a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars with rigid roofs are a class of motor vehicle, some cars rather than all.

clue.text: Visiting Cornish resort, packed a little sun tan concoction and beach accessories

indicators.note: Visiting says the mixture goes inside the resort name

parts.note: Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are blended anew

parts.note: the letters of packed are fodder

indicators.note: a little says take just the opening letter of sun

parts.note: the letters of tan are fodder

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in Cornwall packs some suntan lotion and seaside gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' blends the fodder into CKETANDSPA and 'Visiting' sends that inside the resort; 'a little sun' is just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's pail and shovel for building sandcastles are classic seaside accessories.

clue.text: Fruit imported by Roman governor

indicators.note: imported by says the fruit is carried inside the words that follow, across their join

explanation.surface: A Roman official in a province had a tropical fruit shipped in.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Roman' into the start of 'governor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit with sweet orange flesh, a simple example of fruit.

clue.text: Cleaner from US city answerable to British sovereign

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
under means subordinate to, answerable to a superior
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A cleaner from Los Angeles works as a servant of the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who washes and irons clothes and linen is a cleaner by trade.

clue.text: Two forms of physical punishment? That's laughable

parts.note: a slap with the hand is one punishment
a beating with a stick is the other

explanation.surface: Corporal punishment is mocked as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: comedy built on knockabout blows is meant to be laughed at.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockabout comedy of pratfalls and blows exists to raise laughs, so the comic genre is what's laughable.

clue.text: One wading out of water gets swept back

indicators.note: swept back says the hidden letters are read backwards
out of says the letters are taken from inside the next words, across their join

explanation.surface: Something emerges from water and is carried back by the current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' signals the hidden run TERGE in 'water gets', and 'swept back' turns it round. The draft took 'One wading out' as the definition, but 'out of' is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron-like bird that stalks through shallow water hunting fish is a wader.

clue.text: Seats still available in upper circle for film

definitions.text: Seats still available in upper circle
definitions.meaning: space left at the top of a theatre, in the highest tier of seats
a 1959 British film from the John Braine novel about a social climber

explanation.surface: A box-office notice that tickets remain in the gods for a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1959 film starring Laurence Harvey follows an ambitious man rising through northern English society.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally space remaining in the highest part of the house; also the title of a classic British film.

clue.text: Church leaders share rich spoils

indicators.note: spoils means ruins, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Clergy divide up the wealth they have plundered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like a noun for loot but is a verb meaning ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior priests or bishops who rule in a church are its leaders.

clue.text: A soldier admitted to nearby bar without reason

indicators.note: admitted to says the soldier is let inside the bar word

parts.note: a local is a pub near home, in British usage
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is let into the pub for no apparent reason.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is the British pub nearest where one lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking logic or rational basis means having no reason behind it.

clue.text: Witches brought before judge in English city

indicators.note: brought before places the witches ahead of the judge word

parts.note: a coven is a group of witches
to try is to judge a case in court

explanation.surface: Witches are hauled before a judge in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought before' reads as in court, but it orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A West Midlands cathedral city is a well-known place in England.

clue.text: Drug stashed by children at rear of toilet, moving supply

indicators.note: at rear of puts the children word after the toilet word

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

indicators.note: stashed by says the drug is hidden inside the word for children

parts.note: seed means offspring, descendants
a joint is a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: Kids hide drugs behind the toilet and keep the supply on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is the adverb of supple, not the noun: a loose-jointed body moves supplely.
explanation.definitionFit: Having joints that bend freely means the body moves with suppleness and ease.

clue.text: Angry over Communist uprising in plant

indicators.note: over places the angry word above the next in this down entry

parts.note: mad means angry

indicators.note: uprising says the communist word reads upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a red is a Communist

explanation.surface: Fury over a Communist revolt at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant whose root yields a red dye is a plant species.

clue.text: Plate wife kept in safe

indicators.note: kept in says the wife letter goes inside the safe word

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Plate belonging to a wife is locked in the safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old thieves' slang for a safe, so a safecracker is a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableware made of the grey tin alloy is plate, as in a collection of dishes and vessels.

clue.text: Expert tapes response in European language

indicators.note: tapes means binds round, so the expert word wraps the single letter

parts.note: a geek is an enthusiast expert in a narrow field
R stands for response, as in printed church services

explanation.surface: A specialist records someone's reply in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: In service books V and R mark versicle and response.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of Greece is a language spoken in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Aussie singer's extremely kinky romance?

indicators.note: extremely says take the end letters of kinky

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful untruths, so to lie

explanation.surface: A question about a pop star's reportedly kinky love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' reads as a love affair but is the verb for embroidering the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Kylie Minogue is an Australian pop singer, known everywhere by her first name.

clue.text: Scorn from daughter is precursor to father's temper

indicators.note: precursor to says the word is comes before the father word

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
rage means a fit of temper

explanation.surface: A daughter's contempt comes before her father loses his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn something is to belittle it and speak of it with contempt.

clue.text: The French repulsed in action battling against a region of Spain

indicators.note: against means next to, so the A sits beside the rest
in puts the turned article inside the shuffled letters
battling suggests the letters of action are in conflict and reordered

parts.note: the letters of action are the fodder

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the French article reads backwards

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: French forces were driven back while fighting against a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battling' shuffles the fodder to CATONI; 'repulsed' turns the French article round, and it goes in after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An autonomous community in north-east Spain around Barcelona is a region of the country.

clue.text: Trainee's first in class assessment, defying expectations totally

indicators.note: first in says take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A student comes top of the class, confounding everyone's predictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A young recruit training for the armed forces or police is a trainee.

clue.text: Non-professionals put me down ultimately

parts.note: to lay is to put down or place

indicators.note: ultimately says take the final letter of the word down

explanation.surface: Amateurs dismissing someone with a put-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary people without professional or clerical qualifications are amateurs in a field.

clue.text: Perhaps tape musical introduction to Erasure compilation

indicators.note: introduction says take the opening letter of the word musical
a compilation puts tracks together in a new order, so the band name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cassette with a musical intro to an Erasure greatest-hits album.
explanation.walkthrough: Erasure are a British synth-pop duo; 'tape' is a tape measure, not a cassette.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape measure is one example of a device or person that measures things.
